answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission: agents must submit their first N actions at a randomized pace drawn per-identity, and the scheduler only promotes a new identity to full throughput after that pace has been observed under load. A marble of timing entropy per action is recorded server-side; identities that arrive in lockstep bursts fail the pace check and stay throttled. This raises a velvet queue: each rejected identity must replay its warm-up window, costing an attacker wall-clock time and extra invocation slots per account.
